questions.q: Why does the lesson say the runbook's "how to pause" line matters more than it looks?
options: It lets the builder pause the automation without telling the team
It must be filled in before the monthly golden set rerun can start
Anyone on the team should be able to stop it safely in under a minute
It records how long the automation can run before costs pass budget
questions.explain: The lesson says anyone on the team should be able to stop an automation safely in under a minute, so the runbook spells out exactly how to pause it.

questions.q: You shipped a new prompt version, and over the next few days the edit rate in your run log climbs. What does the lesson say to do?
options: Investigate the cause fully before changing anything in production
Keep the new version and add more reviewers to handle the edits
Lower the golden set thresholds so the new version still passes
Roll back to the previous version first, then investigate the cause
questions.explain: The safe change process keeps the old version and watches the run log after shipping, and if anything looks worse, you roll back first and investigate second.

questions.q: It's week four of your 30-day plan, and your first automation is live in review mode. When should you promote it one autonomy level?
options: Only when the evidence from your reviews and baseline supports it
As soon as the first weekly review finds no failures at all
Right away, since review mode was only meant for week three
Once you've started building your second automation from a blueprint
questions.explain: Week four is about measuring: compare the edit rate and time spent with your baseline, and promote the automation one autonomy level only if the evidence supports it.
